clue.text: This person's into sport in German city

indicators.note: into says the setter's phrase goes inside the word for sport

parts.note: to sport a garment is to wear it
the setter speaking of themself: this person is, so I'm

explanation.surface: The writer is keen on athletics in a city in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sport' reads as athletics but is the verb, to have a garment on. 'This person's' is the setter saying I'm, and 'into' puts that inside. 'in' only links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Weimar is a town in Thuringia, home of Goethe and birthplace of the interwar republic's constitution.

clue.text: Support given to use of whip gets strong adverse reaction

indicators.note: given to says the word for support has the whip stroke attached after it

parts.note: to support someone is to back them
a lash is a stroke with a whip

explanation.surface: Backing for a party whip's tactics draws an angry response.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given to' joins the two pieces in the order printed, and 'gets' leads to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A backlash is a sudden hostile response by many people to a change or event.

clue.text: Wit's sneer's so upsetting — the fellow admits that

indicators.note: admits that says the fellow lets in the jumbled letters just described

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a fellow

indicators.note: upsetting says the words before it are overturned into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped and its S kept

explanation.surface: A clever man's mockery is so distressing, and he himself concedes as much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsetting' rearranges SNEERS SO into ORSESENS, and 'admits that' puts it inside HE. The 's after Wit stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Wit in its older meaning is practical intelligence, and horse sense is plain common judgment, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: British rescue vessel in bay

parts.note: Noah's ark saved his family and the animals from the flood

explanation.surface: A British lifeboat lies in an inlet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bay' looks like the inlet where the vessel lies; it is the verb for a dog's cry. 'in' only links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To bay and to bark are both to give a dog's loud cry, so the verbs are near synonyms.

clue.text: Steal old coin in church collection?

indicators.note: in tells you the coin sits inside the word for the collection

parts.note: the plate is the dish passed round in church for money, and so the offering itself; the question mark admits the stretch
the ecu was an old French silver coin

explanation.surface: Someone pinches an antique coin from the offering at a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: To peculate is to embezzle money entrusted to you, a formal word for theft.

clue.text: Cheers most of the Americans missing start

indicators.note: most of keeps all but the final letter of the short word that follows
missing start says the word for the Americans loses its opening letter

parts.note: Yanks is an informal word for Americans

explanation.surface: A toast is raised to nearly all the Americans who were absent at the beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheers' looks like a toast; it is the British informal word of gratitude. 'most of' cuts THE to TH and 'missing start' cuts YANKS to ANKS.
explanation.definitionFit: In British informal speech cheers is said to express gratitude, an exact synonym.

clue.text: Indian with opinions only partially presented

indicators.note: only partially presented says just a stretch of the two neighbouring words is shown

explanation.surface: A man from India whose views are only given in part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' looks like a mere joining word, but it supplies the first letter of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hopi are a Native American people of north-eastern Arizona, an example of those once called Indians.

clue.text: Noises in the country about new and exciting launch

indicators.note: about puts the farm sounds around the single letter

parts.note: moos are the sounds cows make in the countryside
N is the abbreviation for new, as in NT for New Testament
hot means exciting or thrilling, as in a hot new act

explanation.surface: There is a buzz across the nation over a thrilling new product release.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the country' suggests the nation, but it is farmland where cows are heard. 'about' wraps those sounds round the letter, and 'and' simply joins on the last piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A moonshot is a spacecraft's send-off toward the lunar surface, one kind of rocket lift-off.

clue.text: Excellent article about that time in European capital?

definitions.note: read as a description: located in, or belonging to, one of Europe's chief cities; the question mark flags the example

indicators.note: about wraps the first two pieces round the word for that time

parts.note: A1, written AI in crosswords, means first-rate
then means at that time
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A fine piece of writing concerning that era in a capital city of Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Something Athenian is of or in Athens, the Greek seat of government; the question mark marks one example.

clue.text: Composer wants nothing very loud when singer finally enters

indicators.note: enters says the single letter goes inside the other two pieces

parts.note: O looks like zero
ff is the musical marking fortissimo, very loud

indicators.note: finally takes the closing letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A composer asks for silence, then great volume, as the vocalist at last comes on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes the R of 'singer', and 'enters' slips it between O and FF. 'wants' and 'when' only join the parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Carl Orff was the German who wrote the cantata Carmina Burana.

clue.text: In favour of healthy business surplus

parts.note: pro means for, as in pros and cons
someone fit is in good health

explanation.surface: Someone backs a thriving company having money left over.
explanation.definitionFit: Profit is the money a firm has left once costs are paid, its excess of income over spending.

clue.text: Sacred washing so unnecessary in granting of forgiveness

indicators.note: unnecessary in says the two letters before it are not needed and drop out of the longer word

parts.note: absolution is a priest's formal pardon of sins

explanation.surface: Ritual cleansing is hardly needed when sins are being pardoned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so' reads as an intensifier but is the pair of letters to remove: 'unnecessary in' takes SO out of ABSOLUTION.
explanation.definitionFit: An ablution is a ritual cleansing of the body or of vessels in a religious ceremony.

clue.text: Attention given to female anxiety

indicators.note: given to says the word for attention is attached to the letter for female, which goes in front

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for female on forms
to give ear, or lend an ear, is to pay attention

explanation.surface: Care is devoted to a woman's worries.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name a state of dread or worry, near synonyms.

clue.text: Time in driver's training device that may raise pulse rate?

definitions.note: read as a noun phrase: something that may speed up the heartbeat

indicators.note: in says the single letter sits inside the word for the training rig

parts.note: a simulator is a machine that mimics a car or cockpit so learners can practise
T is the physics abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Hours spent in a learner motorist's practice rig can set the heart racing.
explanation.definitionFit: A stimulator is something that excites the body into activity, and a quicker heartbeat is one such effect.

clue.text: Attempt to eat meat, prime bit of expensive rubbish

indicators.note: to eat makes the word for attempt swallow the pieces that follow

parts.note: a try is an attempt
rump is a cut of beef, as in rump steak

indicators.note: prime bit of picks the leading letter of the word after it

explanation.surface: Someone tries a cut of pricey steak that proves to be garbage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prime' looks like praise for the meat; 'prime bit of' takes only the opening letter of 'expensive'. 'to eat' makes TRY the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Trumpery is showy but worthless stuff, or nonsense, a dated synonym for trash.

clue.text: Like traditional countryman seen as robust, ultimately getting scrawny

indicators.note: getting says that closing letter has the word for scrawny added after it
ultimately takes the closing letter of the word before it

parts.note: weedy means thin and puny

explanation.surface: A rustic old gent once thought sturdy ends up thin and bony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' takes the T of 'robust' and 'getting' adds the next piece. Tweed is the rough woollen cloth of the old-fashioned British country gentleman.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes someone given to wearing rough woollen suits, the mark of the old-fashioned rural gentleman.

clue.text: Bit of poetry event is cut

indicators.note: cut says the short word before it is removed from the word for event

parts.note: an episode is an incident or event

explanation.surface: A stretch of a verse recital has been trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' looks like a plain verb but is the pair of letters that 'cut' removes from EPISODE.
explanation.definitionFit: An epode is the third section of a Greek ode, following the strophe and antistrophe.

clue.text: Uncle's aim, after training, is to be virile

indicators.note: after training suggests the letters before it have been drilled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped and its S kept

explanation.surface: After working out, an uncle hopes to be manly.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads the apostrophe-s as 'uncle is', but that S is one of the letters 'after training' rearranges. 'is to be' only leads to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Both adjectives mean having manly strength and vigour.

clue.text: 'Baddie' artist's termed — not half

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a member of Britain's Royal Academy of Arts; the possessive adds the S

indicators.note: not half says only half of the word for termed is kept, here its front half

parts.note: termed means called, given a name

explanation.surface: A painter is labelled a villain, and how!
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' is British slang for 'very much so'; here it literally keeps the first half of CALLED, which is CAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A rascal is a rogue or scoundrel, the villain a child would call by that nursery word.

clue.text: Defensive attitude is nonsense, leading to awful enmity later

indicators.note: leading to says the word for nonsense comes first, ahead of the jumbled part

parts.note: bunk, short for bunkum, means nonsense

indicators.note: awful suggests the two words after it are in a bad state and need rearranging

explanation.surface: Being on the defensive is foolish and brings terrible hostility afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface takes 'awful' as describing the hostility; it is the anagram signal for the eleven letters after it. 'leading to' only fixes the order of the two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the embattled, self-protective outlook of people who feel under attack.

clue.text: Response when Conservative rises in the world

indicators.note: in a down entry rises means the letter climbs toward the top of the word

parts.note: a reaction is a response
C is the abbreviation for Conservative, the British political party

explanation.surface: How people respond when a Tory climbs the social ladder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rises' lifts the C of REACTION to the top of this down entry. 'when' and 'in' only join the parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Creation means everything that exists, the universe, a synonym in that broad sense.

clue.text: Country in the Balance — yen for end of war?

indicators.note: for says the letter for yen takes the place of the letter picked from war

parts.note: Libra, the zodiac sign of the scales, is also called the Balance

indicators.note: end of picks the closing letter of the word after it

parts.note: Y is the abbreviation for yen, the Japanese currency

explanation.surface: A nation's fate is uncertain, and it longs for the fighting to stop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yen' reads as a longing but is the currency, Y. 'for' swaps it in for the R that 'end of' takes from 'war', inside LIBRA.
explanation.definitionFit: Libya is a North African state on the Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: Remove newspaper headline after success in industrial negotiations?

definitions.meaning: to delete a name from a list or register, as a doctor is taken from the medical roll

definitions.text: newspaper headline after success in industrial negotiations?
definitions.meaning: a whimsical banner in terse press style announcing that a planned walkout has been cancelled once talks succeed

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to delete from a register, and its two words also make a terse announcement that a walkout is cancelled.

clue.text: Coats etc. were untidily packed in a tour abroad

indicators.note: packed in says the jumbled short word is stowed inside the other jumbled pair
abroad, in its old meaning of astray or wide of the mark, signals the two words before it are rearranged
untidily says the word before it is put in a messy new order

explanation.surface: Jackets and the like were stuffed messily into luggage on a foreign trip.
explanation.walkthrough: There are two separate anagrams, each with its own signal: 'untidily' for the word before it and 'abroad' for the pair before it. 'packed in' nests one inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Outerwear is clothing worn over other garments outdoors, such as jackets and overcoats.

clue.text: Ask other cooks initially to bake this?

definitions.note: this points back at the whole clue: something you might get other cooks to bake

indicators.note: to bake suggests the ingredients before it are mixed and cooked into something new
initially takes the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: You request that the rest of the kitchen staff start by making a particular treat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to bake' rearranges ASK OTHER plus the C that 'initially' takes from 'cooks'. The whole clue then describes the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortcake is a crumbly biscuit or dessert base made in an oven, which is all the request describes.

clue.text: Horror and calamity unending around Turkey's capital

indicators.note: around wraps the shortened word for calamity about the single letter
unending says the word for calamity loses its final letter

parts.note: a disaster is a calamity

indicators.note: capital here means the capital letter that opens the word before it

explanation.surface: Terror and catastrophe without end surround Ankara.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turkey's capital' is not Ankara but the first letter of Turkey. 'unending' trims DISASTER to DISASTE, and 'around' places that about the T.
explanation.definitionFit: Distaste is aversion or dislike, a milder cousin of the revulsion that horror can mean.

clue.text: Apartment housing a French exhibit prominently

indicators.note: housing says the word for apartment holds the French word inside it

parts.note: flat is the British word for an apartment
un is the French for a

explanation.surface: A flat is home to a notable show from France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exhibit' reads as a noun, a show, but is the verb to display; 'housing' is the container signal, not a home.
explanation.definitionFit: To flaunt something is to show it off ostentatiously.

clue.text: Arrange to host university seminar?

indicators.note: to host makes the word for arrange take the single letter inside it

parts.note: to form troops into a line is to arrange them

explanation.surface: Someone organises putting on a college discussion class.
explanation.definitionFit: A forum is a meeting for open discussion, and a tutorial class is one example, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Love to lead congregation as in the past

indicators.note: to lead says the letter for love goes in front of the word for congregation

parts.note: love is a score of zero in tennis, written O
a church's fold is its flock of worshippers

explanation.surface: Someone delights in heading a church's worshippers the way it used to be done.
explanation.definitionFit: The literary phrase means formerly or long ago, as in 'days of old'.
